lessons.title: Two-dimensional period is not equal to two-dimensional space
lessons.summary: plane group acts on a two-dimensional pattern; layer group acts on an object in three-dimensional space, but has only two independent periodic translations. layer group can include the operation of flipping the normal direction. The 17 plane groups and 80 layer group in the textbook answer different questions.

sections.title: Specify periodic directions first
sections.text: plane group acts on a two-dimensional pattern; layer group acts on an object in three-dimensional space, but has only two independent periodic translations. layer group can include the operation of flipping the normal direction. The 17 plane groups and 80 layer group in the textbook answer different questions.

sections.title: Write boundaries into matching rules
sections.text: Reduce in-plane coordinates modulo the two lattice vectors, but do not reduce the normal coordinate modulo a period. A vacuum-containing 3D periodic cell is a computational representation of a film; its full supercell translations are not automatically physical operations of an isolated film.

sections.title: Check for a real mapping
sections.text: Cut layers from a simple cubic parent, enumerate matrices preserving the plane orientation, then find in-plane translations. Every atom must map to one with the same label, and the complete map must be bijective.

lessons.title: Cut planes, terminations, and exchange of the two sides
lessons.summary: (001),(110),(111) have different in-plane metrics. A normal alone does not specify atomic termination; composition, layer count and cutting origin are structural inputs too.

sections.title: Geometric surface and concrete surface
sections.text: (001),(110),(111) have different in-plane metrics. A normal alone does not specify atomic termination; composition, layer count and cutting origin are structural inputs too.

sections.title: Identify the operation of flipping the normal direction
sections.text: Rn=−n swaps both sides of the membrane. It is possible to maintain a symmetric film but destroy adsorbed labels or heterogeneous interfaces on only one side; this is not determined by the group sign alone.

sections.title: Character that maintains momentum and spin
sections.text: In orthonormal Cartesian coordinates, wave vectors transform by R; axial spins acquire an extra det(R). Time reversal reverses both k and spin without moving atoms.

lessons.title: Stacking path and interface common symmetry
lessons.summary: The upper half layer is continuously translated along the in-plane basis vector, and the mapping of all atoms for each operation is compared. Interface common symmetry also relies on lateral registration, you cannot just compare the abstract point group names on both sides.

sections.title: Compare two sides using the same in-plane lattice
sections.text: The upper half layer is continuously translated along the in-plane basis vector, and the mapping of all atoms for each operation is compared. Interface common symmetry also relies on lateral registration, you cannot just compare the abstract point group names on both sides.

sections.title: Tracking special registration points
sections.text: General disregistry may remove operations, while special alignment restores some. The seven-point curve records samples and need not find every special position; other fractional disregistries can be entered manually.

sections.title: Connect symmetry permission to physical properties
sections.text: Bring the retention operation to the physical-property tensor class to continue to constrain the response components; operation reduction does not guarantee that a certain response will become larger, nor does it replace microscopic material parameters.

lessons.title: Structural mirror images and proper-rotation alignment
lessons.summary: active mirror changes configuration. Passive change of basis only changes the coordinates of the same configuration, but must also transform the lattice and manipulation matrix. This experiment uses an explicit inverse sign of x to generate a mirror image.

sections.title: distinguishes active mirroring from coordinate description
sections.text: active mirror changes configuration. Passive change of basis only changes the coordinates of the same configuration, but must also transform the lattice and manipulation matrix. This experiment uses an explicit inverse sign of x to generate a mirror image.

sections.title: only allows direction-preserving rigid body registration
sections.text: enumerates all correspondences of the same type of atoms, and then finds the best rotation of the determinant +1. Different labels cannot be interchanged. A registration residual of zero indicates that this finite set of points and the mirror image can be coincident.

sections.title: returns to the level of space group
sections.text: chirality crystal structure can only have orientation-preserving operations, involving 65 Sohncke groups; 22 of them form 11 pairs of enantiogroups. The remaining Sohncke group types can also accommodate the chirality structure.

lessons.title: chirality , polarity Different issues with ferroelectricity
lessons.summary: polar vector must be maintained by each group operation. By combining all (R−I) constraints, the dimensions of the allowed directions can be obtained; the D3 prototype is zero, and the C4v cone only allows the axial direction.

sections.title: Directly solve for allowed polar vectors
sections.text: polar vector must be maintained by each group operation. By combining all (R−I) constraints, the dimensions of the allowed directions can be obtained; the D3 prototype is zero, and the C4v cone only allows the axial direction.

sections.title: chirality and polarity are verified separately
sections.text: A D3 point set can be chiral but nonpolar. A C4v pyramid can be polar but achiral because of mirrors. Absence of inversion does not replace these independent tests.

sections.title: discusses responses using independent experiments
sections.text: polarity only states the symmetry permission, but does not give the spontaneous polarization size or reversible switching. The polarization round trip model uses an imposed rotation angle and specifies the natural optical rotation and Faraday's round trip convention.

lessons.title: Tolerance, pseudo-symmetry and reverse identification
lessons.summary: adds a known amplitude to the ideal point set along a fixed perturbation direction. Strict symmetries of the current configuration are recorded separately from approximations of the ideal parent configuration; geometric errors use the model length.

sections.title: Quantify the actual displacements first
sections.text: adds a known amplitude to the ideal point set along a fixed perturbation direction. Strict symmetries of the current configuration are recorded separately from approximations of the ideal parent configuration; geometric errors use the model length.

sections.title: When accepting a collection, check the closure
sections.text: Passing the distance threshold on a per-operation basis does not automatically guarantee that the combination will also pass. A tolerance scan displays the accepted number and the maximum residual for each candidate, without outputting the strict group name when closure fails.

sections.title: Excluding candidates from limited evidence
sections.text: Test chirality, allowed polar vectors, inversion and other properties in sequence, retaining candidates consistent with all known evidence. One remaining teaching candidate does not prove an arbitrary real material structure.

lessons.title: From valence bonds to the AKLT parent Hamiltonian
lessons.summary: The AKLT picture projects two virtual spin-1/2 objects at each site into symmetric spin 1; neighboring virtual spins form singlets. This connects the existing permutation and CG lessons.

sections.title: Project two virtual spins into spin 1
sections.text: The AKLT picture projects two virtual spin-1/2 objects at each site into symmetric spin 1; neighboring virtual spins form singlets. This connects the existing permutation and CG lessons.

sections.title: Construct every bond
sections.text: Two spin-1 particles combine to total spin 0,1,2. S·S has eigenvalues −2,−1,1; this page’s bond operator is zero in the first two sectors and 2 in total spin 2.

sections.title: Boundary changes in low-energy space
sections.text: Periodic and open chains use different bond sets. An ideal open chain has a four-dimensional ground space from edge degrees of freedom. Recalculate under finite perturbations rather than assuming exact degeneracy persists.

lessons.title: Schmidt decomposition, entanglement spectrum and projective representation
lessons.summary: First explain the boundary and ground state degeneracy. The projection choice on the degenerate subspace on this page determines the pure state; other edge states may give different finite chain entanglement spectra.

sections.title: Explicitly selected quantum state
sections.text: First explain the boundary and ground state degeneracy. The projection choice on the degenerate subspace on this page determines the pure state; other edge states may give different finite chain entanglement spectra.

sections.title: Get probability from coefficient matrix
sections.text: Reshape the wavefunction coefficients across the bipartition and perform a singular value decomposition. The squared singular values are the Schmidt probabilities and sum to 1. This page uses the natural logarithm ln and reports entropy in nats; the density-matrix experiment uses log₂ and bits. Divide this page's value by ln(2) to obtain bits. The same distribution (1/2,1/2) gives ln(2) nat = 1 bit. The overall state here must be the selected pure state; the coefficient-matrix Schmidt construction cannot be applied directly to a mixed state.

sections.title: Identify the group action on virtual space
sections.text: Virtual π rotations at the AKLT point can be represented by Pauli matrices. They anticommute, while corresponding physical integer-spin D2 operations commute, illustrating linear versus projective representations.

lessons.title: Disturbance path and protection conditions
lessons.summary: Time reversal is antiunitary and requires complex-conjugating H. Spatial inversion exchanges sites rather than merely reversing spins. A uniform tilted field may preserve inversion; a gradient field can additionally break it.

sections.title: Verify each protection operation separately
sections.text: Time reversal is antiunitary and requires complex-conjugating H. Spatial inversion exchanges sites rather than merely reversing spins. A uniform tilted field may preserve inversion; a gradient field can additionally break it.

sections.title: Record the same set of diagnostics along the path
sections.text: fixes the chain length, boundary and other parameters, only changes D or h, and links the low energy spacing, ground state space dimension and four symmetric residuals. The passed symmetry can be directly verified by the numerical residuals.

sections.title: Distinguish between limited observations and bulk conclusions
sections.text: Finite chains do not have strict thermodynamic phase transition diagnostics. Size, boundary and protection conditions need to be compared; this site does not automatically translate energy level changes into bulk topology labels during general disturbances.

cases.title: Three surface cuts of a cubic parent
cases.summary: Compare in-plane lattices and inherited parent operations for 001,110,111 cuts.
cases.assumption: A monatomic simple-cubic parent, not a relaxed surface of a specific element.

cases.title: Heterostructure layers and lateral stacking
cases.summary: Distinguish each side's own symmetry from the operations common to the complete interface.
cases.assumption: Chemical label prototype of the same in-plane lattice, does not simulate actual lattice mismatch or energy bands.

cases.title: Single-sided adsorption and surface marking
cases.summary: Checks if the upper and lower surfaces are still swappable with an element tag with only one side.
cases.assumption: tag only changes the label, but does not include adsorption mechanics, surface charge and structural relaxation.

cases.title: quartz: Differentiation between chirality and non- polarity
cases.summary: Using quartz point group 32 as context, find allowed polar vectors for a finite D3 point set.
cases.assumption: only reproduces the constraints at the point group level, not the quartz primitive cell , nor does it predict the optical rotation coefficient.

cases.title: Tetragonal polar structures: allowed polarity versus switching
cases.summary: Use the C4v prototype to distinguish a polar axis, mirror planes and evidence for electric-field switching.
cases.assumption: The pyramid is not a BaTiO3 primitive cell. Berry polarization and ferroelectric switching barriers are not calculated.

cases.title: Structural optimization residuals and pseudo-symmetry
cases.summary: adjusts controllable small displacements separately from recognition thresholds, preserving distance evidence for each candidate.
cases.assumption: Parent configuration candidate check for finite point sets; any POSCAR/CIF are still handled by existing structure tools.

cases.title: AKLT valence bond solid
cases.summary: Connect virtual spins, exchange projectors, finite-chain ground states and entanglement.
cases.assumption: model is a theoretical fixed point and does not fit the exchange parameters of real spin chain materials.

cases.title: Haldane chain and edge degrees of freedom
cases.summary: compares periodic and open boundaries, and observes the impact of edge space and pure state selection on entanglement .
cases.assumption: An AKLT chain with N=3–5; its small-chain spectrum is not an experimental spectrum in the thermodynamic limit.

cases.title: Anisotropy and symmetry-breaking field paths
cases.summary: Point-by-point tracking of symmetry residuals, low energy spacing and protection conditions.
cases.assumption: A finite seven-point path cannot replace the infinite-chain phase diagram. General perturbations do not automatically classify SPT phases.
